chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem that the man sleeps between two slave girls and two free women. Indeed, your women are at the status of playthings.

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: At the status of / in the position of

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man sleeping with multiple wives or concubines according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter of miscellaneous rulings, this hadith clarifies the permissibility of a man sleeping between two slave girls and two free women, reflecting the juristic distinctions in marital and concubinage arrangements during the early Islamic period. The concluding metaphor describing women as 'playthings' (لُعَب) is interpreted by Shia scholars not merely as objectification, but as indicating their role as sources of comfort, amusement, and companionship within the domestic sphere, emphasizing the relational aspect of the bond.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem that the man sleeps between two slave girls and two free women. But rather, your women are at the status of the playthings’.
en.sarwar: 16. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not unlawful to sleep between the two of your slave-girls or free wives; your women are like dolls.’”
